Parasites travel from the bite to the liver, then invade red blood cells, causing fever, chills, headaches, nausea, fatigue, and anemia; severe P. falciparum infections can lead to seizures, kidney failure, or coma. Transmission is not through casual contact, though rare routes include mother-to-child transmission or contaminated blood transfusions. Prevention emphasizes avoiding bites and eliminating standing water; diagnosis is by blood tests, and treatment depends on species and infection severity.

articleSummary: Goiás, Brazil, reports more than 11,000 chikungunya cases since January 2026, a 383% rise from the same period last year, with deaths increasing from 2 to 7. articleSummary: In Langkat Regency, North Sumatra, Indonesia, researchers studied two villages in Desa Ujung Bandar, Salapian district, amid palm-oil plantations and disturbed forests. From July 2022 to June 2023, four nightly human landing catches (18:30–06:00) yielded 597 mosquitoes: 584 were Anopheles dirus and 13 Anopheles scanloni. DNA testing found six An. dirus carrying malaria parasite DNA, including Plasmodium knowlesi in three specimens (about 0.5% of those tested) and Plasmodium vivax in four; all An. scanloni tested were parasite-free. This provides the first evidence of An. dirus and An. scanloni in Sumatra and suggests An. dirus as a potential vector for knowlesi malaria there, though DNA presence does not prove transmission. The finding expands knowlesi’s distribution beyond prior sites and highlights the need for further ecological and entomological studies on vector behavior in Sumatra, where North Sumatra reported 377 knowlesi cases in 2017.
notes: 本記事は研究論文の報道であり、実際のヒト感染症例の急増を示すものではない。DNA検出は感染伝播の証明ではない点に留意。北スマトラでは2017年に377例のknowlesiマラリア症例が報告されており、媒介蚊の生態研究として継続的な監視が望ましい。

articleHeadline: Ebola Cases in Congo Surpass 10,000 as Fastest-Growing Outbreak on Record Spreads With No Approved Vaccine
articleSummary: DR Congo’s Ebola outbreak has surpassed 10,000 confirmed cases—the largest and fastest-growing in the nation—caused by the Bundibugyo virus, a rare strain with no approved vaccine or treatment. Ituri remains the epicenter, with over 70% of cases across eight provinces and 66 health zones reporting infections. Violence, mistrust and displacement hinder response; about 40 of the 46 most recent deaths occurred outside treatment centers, and more than 70% of new infections were outside known contact lists. The first clinical trial, TUMAINI, tests Ervebo against Bundibugyo at sites such as Rwampara Hospital in Ituri. Uganda has reported 20 imported cases; Kenya and Nigeria have also seen cases. Transmission is via bodily fluids; rapid detection improves survival.

articleHeadline: Mắc cúm A, tùy tiện dùng Tamiflu có thể gây hại
articleSummary: Influenza A management in Vietnam cautions against indiscriminate use of oseltamivir (Tamiflu). Most influenza A infections are mild and resolve in about a week, but severe disease and complications can occur, especially in high-risk groups: children under 5 (especially under 2), adults 65+, and those with cardiovascular disease, asthma, COPD, diabetes, liver or kidney disease, or neurological conditions. Immunocompromised individuals (cancer treatment, organ transplantation, HIV, long-term immunosuppression) and pregnant women or up to two weeks postpartum are at higher risk. Obesity (BMI ≥40), under-19 on long-term aspirin, and residents of long-term care facilities also require evaluation. Tamiflu should be considered early for severe cases or high-risk patients, ideally within 48 hours; healthy mild cases benefit from supportive care. Self-medication and dosing errors risk adverse effects; seek urgent care for severe symptoms. Vaccination and hygiene remain key; vaccine efficacy can reach ~90% under optimal conditions, varying by strain.
